title: Causal E5M2 flash attention with published row statistics
formula: out = (E5M2(exp(Q @ K^T / sqrt(128) - rowmax)) @ V) / rowsum with top-left causal masking per head, 128x128 tiles; E5M2 [BH*S1,128] Q and [BH*S2,128] K/V -> float32 [BH*S1,128] out plus float32 [BH*S1] rowmax and rowsum, where rowsum is the FP32 probability sum taken before the cast
study_for: The causal boundary is rebuilt, never stored: `apply_causal_diagonal_sb0` fills a `MaskReg` from `cols.arange(...)` and one `compare`, then `select`s the masked lanes to `NEG_LARGE`. Nothing keeps a predicate in memory between tiles.

It is written twice, and the diff is the lesson: `_sb0` compares against `r + 1` and `_sb1` against `r + ROWS_PER_SB + 1`. Each vector sub-block owns a different 64-row band, so the diagonal offset is part of the body rather than a parameter — specialise per sub-block, do not branch inside the loop.
The N tail gets its own mask pass (`apply_n_tail_mask_multi`), kept separate from the diagonal so a tail tile pays for one and a diagonal tile for the other.

`rowmax` and `rowsum` are public outputs, not debug state, and main.py compares them three orders of magnitude tighter than `out`. They are FP32 quantities defined before any E5M2 cast, so a wrong mask or a wrong score scale lands on rowmax instead of disappearing into the quantization noise of the result, and a denominator summed after the cast fails on rowsum alone.
do_not_copy_when: Your mask comes from runtime data rather than from the row index. `arange` + `compare` rebuilds a mask that is a FUNCTION of position; a data-dependent predicate needs the values on hand, and no unit in this gallery demonstrates that yet.

Your query tile is not 128 rows split 64/64 across the two vector sub-blocks. `ROWS_PER_SB = TILE_M // 2` is wired into both diagonal bodies, into the row-state addressing and into the eight-float head stride the row statistics are padded to so that each head and sub-block starts on a 32-byte GM transaction boundary — that padding is output-owned and sliced off by the host in main.py, and a copier who keeps the compact shape inherits the write conflict it exists to prevent.
